$comment: Size ratchets (PHASE-0 T2). Every path below may only SHRINK: check-ratchets.mjs fails the build when a listed file exceeds its pinned line count (wc -l, i.e. newlines). Seeded 2026-07-27 at commit 8a37099 from measured wc -l on a clean, instrument-free tree. Entries: every tracked *.ts/*.tsx under packages/*/src/ or watchdog/src/ (excluding __tests__, *.test.*, *.spec.*, db/migrations) that already exceeded maxNewFileLines. The 15 files the overhaul plan names are all here; the rest were seeded because the new-file rule would otherwise fail them on day one. To LOWER entries after real deletion: node deploy/checks/check-ratchets.mjs --tighten. To RAISE one, or to add a new file above the cap, edit this file BY HAND in a gate-side-only commit — that edit is meant to be seen and reviewed. No tool raises a number.

$raises.why: The fan-out join is +551 lines of the ONE writer, and it cannot live anywhere else: `single-writer-conformance.test.ts` keeps an EMPTY allowlist for `work`/`work_events`/`adjudications`, so a second module holding `openDelegationJoin`/`landPiece` fails the walk, and the only way to make it pass would be the move the walk exists to refuse. What it BUYS is a bigger cut elsewhere in the same commit: `a2a-transport.ts` 2037 -> 1773 (-264) and `loop.ts` 9336 -> 9341 net after the delegation rewrite, with the park string machine gone entirely. T3's report flagged this exact growth and asked, at T9, whether the walk should learn about a `work/` DIRECTORY rather than a file; that question is now overdue and is the real fix.

THE iMESSAGE DOOR, plus its two attachment siblings and the two platform sends that live in this file (sendAlert, the busy-ack). This is the largest single raise of the task and it is the one that buys the most: this file is the transport EVERY iMessage in the product passes through — the auto-route, the imessage_send tool, alerts, the busy-ack, the first-run welcome, the healer's approval prompt, the A2A owner hand-back — and before it, only the first two produced a ledger row and only when the caller had already decided the send worked. Recording here closes six of PINNED s8's unrecorded paths at one physical point instead of six. The two attachment siblings are wrapped for a named reason: sendIMessageWithAttachment calls sendIMessage for the caption, so without one scope over the pair every captioned file would have written TWO rows for one thing the person received.

The engine's ten evidence-writing sites become identity DECLARATIONS. persistRoutingMarker lost its delivery parameter entirely (a net deletion inside this file) and each auto-route / engine-ack branch gained a `withOutboundAsync` wrapper around the send it was already making. The scope wrappers cost more lines than the argument objects they replaced, and what they buy is that the loop can no longer claim a delivery: the row is written by the transport from what it observed, which is what makes `outcome='failed'` expressible for the first time.

The boot reconciliation's THIRD outcome, which `index.ts` named as owed to T5 in its own comment. Deliveries are universal now, so `was this ask answered` is a recorded edge rather than an inference, and an ask whose claiming turn DELIVERED and was then killed is closed pointing at that delivery instead of being re-answered (re-serving a question the person already had answered) or held forever. Still the ONE writer of `work.state`; the single-writer walk's allowlist is still EMPTY. The `work/` DIRECTORY question T3 raised and T4 repeated is now three tasks old and belongs to T9.

ONE outbound scope per send-tool call, opened at the single dispatch door every path already goes through — the same place and the same reasoning as the P6a tool-call identity that sits three lines above it. This is what closes the ten unrecorded send paths in ONE change instead of ten: `gmail_reply`, `gmail_forward`, `outlook_reply`, `outlook_forward`, `teams_send_message`, `teams_send_channel_message` and `voice_call` are now recorded without any of them being named anywhere. The alias-resolution tail was extracted to `dispatchResolved` so the scope can wrap it; that extraction is most of the count.

The T4/T5 collision, resolved by ROUTING rather than duplicating. T4 recorded the join relay with its own `recordDelivery` call; T5 puts a recorder on the dashboard, iMessage, SMS and provider doors that same relay pushes through, so leaving both would have written TWO rows for one relay. The relay now declares its identity once and every door it crosses folds into that single row. `recordPieceDelivery` is routed through the same door recorder for the same reason. Against this: the file is still 238 lines below where T4 found it (2037 at the phase base).

THE BROWSER SPEECH-OUT DOOR, on both engine tiers (OR3 keeps both, so both are instrumented). Research 03 measured voice as recording NOTHING on either path. One row per BURST rather than per clause — the clause queue is how one reply is transported, not several replies — recorded where synthesis actually starts, so a turn whose text sanitizes to nothing speakable never claims a delivery, and corrected to `failed` if the stream dies mid-reply.

THE PHONE SPEECH-OUT DOOR. Research 03 named `every spoken utterance in call-session.ts` among the paths recording nothing. Inside the outbound scope the auto-route declares, the sentences of one reply fold into ONE row; outside a scope (the call's own opener) an utterance stands as its own row.

The healer's approval prompt reaches the owner's phone and recorded nothing (research 03 names `approval-routing:473`). Six lines: it declares itself a PLATFORM outbound rather than an agent's, because the healer speaks for the box.
Two lines: the boot crash-reconciliation log now reports the third outcome it can produce. The comment above it stops saying T5 owes this rekey, because T5 landed it.

Not a raise — a first PIN, at the count the growth detector caught. `linkArtifactsToDelivery` lands here because this module is the sole owner of `turn_artifacts` writes, and the Phase-1 exit named `turn_artifacts.delivery_id` as a Phase-2 debt that must not be closed half-way. Putting the write anywhere else would give that table a second writer to pay for a column, which is the disease. Pinned decrease-only from here.

A NEW file above the 400-line cap, pinned deliberately rather than split. What it holds is ONE mechanism with no seam in it: a send declares an identity, the transport it passes through records the outcome, and the receipt writer links itself to that same row — three parties to one scope, and splitting them puts an import cycle between the scope and its own doors. Roughly half the count is the reasoning: which clause of the dashboard predicate exists for which observed defect, why `held` needs a named entry point instead of a door, why a failure downgrades and a success never upgrades. That text is the reason the next reader can tell an honest ledger from a convenient one, and stripping it to reach 400 would be the arithmetic-over-functionality move the owner ruled out on 2026-07-26. Pinned decrease-only from here; the honest shrink is PHASE-4's, when OR2 removes the engine-ack lane this file currently has to describe.

+15 for the receipt-ordering fix in `25d83d4`. The iMessage and SMS auto-routes wrote their C26 receipt ONE STATEMENT below the outbound scope that had just recorded the send, so `deliveries.receipt_id` read 0 of 119 on the live ledger and would have shipped as the written-only column the Phase-1 exit named as the failure mode to avoid. Both receipts moved inside their scope callback, which costs a closure and the paragraph explaining why the placement is load-bearing. Caught by counting rows on the box, not by reading the diff — the comment says so, because the next person to move one of these lines needs to know what it breaks.

PHASE-2 T6's five in-loop rekeys, net +117 after a trim pass that moved the reasoning to the module it belongs to. What LANDED here cannot live elsewhere: these are gates INSIDE the turn, and each one now reads a record where it used to compute an answer for itself — the redundant-closeout floor (the prose classifier is DELETED and the authority is the delivery ledger), the silent-closeout owe-filter, the turn-record's FIRST READER at finalize (R-0: `finalizeTurn` has always written the true outcome and NOTHING read it), the waiting-on-owner disposition and its reopen edge, and the settled read collapsing from an array-build to one query. What it BUYS, measured in the same task: `classifiers/output.ts` -24 (the twenty-phrase CLOSEOUT regex and its two consts, gone), `memory/directive.ts` -4 net on the selector with R-2 closed (a four-line JSON-shape probe becomes `answer_message_id IS NULL`), one dead flag stripped, and four hand-rolled copies of the answered-edge read replaced by calls. The line count is the wrong meter for this one and the plan says so (#7): what to read is the demolition ledger.

+54 for `abandonUnservableAsks()` — requirement 2b's THIRD cause of `abandoned`, and it must be in this module because `transition()` is the only writer of `work.state` and the single-writer walk's Part A allowlist is EMPTY. It disposes of tickets nobody can ever serve or close (no conversation identity, or a root message that no longer exists); 74 such rows on the dev box got their one-shot honest disposition at boot, 25 identity-less and 49 gone-root, each with its reason on its own `work_events` row. THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE TASK TO RAISE THIS FILE (T3 590->1145, T4, T5 1175, now 1229). The real fix is the question T3 asked and T4 and T5 repeated: should the single-module walk learn about a `work/` DIRECTORY? T9 owns that ruling and it is now four tasks overdue.

+26, all of it ONE structural clause and the measurement that justifies it. `isOwnerAsk` now requires the row to carry a CHANNEL, because OR4 says channel/sender/trust/lane are stamped at INGEST and a `role='user'` row without one did not come through a door — it is the platform writing to itself in the second person. Three producers were doing exactly that (the PM's own situation report, the [ENGINE RENAME REQUEST], a spawned agent's kickoff), each opening an owner ask ticket nobody could ever serve, and the PM was being told THE OWNER was talking to it. The comment carries the query and its result because the evidence is the whole argument: every genuine ask on this box carries channel+sender+meta+conversation, every stuck one carries none of the four.

+12: the boot sweep that gives unservable ask tickets an honest terminal state, placed beside the crash reconciliation it belongs with (both answer 'what did a restart inherit that nobody can finish'). Twelve lines and a `try` — there is no smaller honest form.

+6 in `resolveCompilePendingJoins`, which T4's report named as owed to T6 BY NAME. The site stops holding its own reading of the answered edge and calls the one reader, which also means it now sees the ticket's `result_delivery_id` before the mig-113 stamp — strictly more evidence for the same decision. The +6 is the receipt appearing in the settle's reason string plus the two-line explanation of why `done` still is not asserted here.

NEW FILE, above the 400-line cap, and the addition is meant to be argued with. It is THE ANSWERED EDGE: the one place this tree answers 'has the person heard from us', replacing seven mechanisms that each answered it for themselves (a twenty-phrase prose classifier, two turn-local booleans, a legacy status scan joined by hand to a message column, an array the loop had to BUILD to learn a boolean, a loop-local variable set at four sites, `conv_key IS NULL`, `swept_at`) plus the turn record's own `exit_reason`, which finalizeTurn has always written and nothing read (R-0). Roughly two thirds of it is the argument, the measurements and the requirement-preserved lines — deliberately, because the danger with this particular collapse is not that it is wrong today but that somebody loosens a key later without knowing which incident bought it. Splitting it would put the answer-receipt read in one file and the closeout-owe read in another, which is the exact split requirement 2d exists to end.

The commitment half of requirement 4a — `openCommitment` / `resolveCommitment` / `dismissCommitment` and the three obligation reads — and it cannot live anywhere else for the same structural reason T4's raise gives: `single-writer-conformance.test.ts` PART A holds an EMPTY allowlist for `work`, so a second module writing commitment rows fails the walk. What this raise BUYS, measured in the same commit: `memory/open-loops.ts` is DELETED ENTIRELY (623 lines — the fenced-section parser, the Jaccard/coverage matcher, the store-contradiction regex guard, the party-attribution map and both renderers), its unit test goes with it (321 lines), and the `open_loops` table is dropped by migration 136. The two renderers come back as `work/obligations.ts`, a READ-ONLY module of 118 lines. The T3/T4 question stands and is now overdue: the walk should learn about a `work/` DIRECTORY rather than a single file (T9).

`loop_resolve` (one verb, 18 lines of definition + 11 of dispatch) becomes `commitment_open` + `commitment_resolve` (two verbs, 37 + 68). The extra verb is the point of the task and not an accident: the deleted module had a RESOLUTION verb only, because a PARSER created the rows. Delete the parser without adding a creation door and the capability is deleted, not replaced — so the requirement-preserved line ('a promise the agent makes is tracked until it is delivered or dropped') would have been a lie. The dispatch is longer than the one it replaces because it refuses in three named ways the old one could not: outside a turn, on an id that does not resolve, and — the load-bearing one — on `kept` with no delivery recorded for the turn. PHASE-2 T8 absorbs both verbs into `work_open`/`work_close_request` with alias rows; `tools/aliases.ts:76-86` is the mechanism and it already exists.

+6 lines at ONE site: the per-turn OPEN LOOPS injection becomes the OPEN WORK injection, and the added lines are the comment recording why the block is keyed on `conversation_id` rather than on `conv_key` (the deleted block compared conv_key strings — the column that also carried the claim token and the park sigils, so a parked row changed which party its items belonged to). A NEW file above the 400-line new-file cap, added to `files` deliberately so the addition is seen and argued with. It is the tracker's WRITE side on the spine: creation, the typed attribute patcher, and `setTrackerStatus` (= `transition()` with the tracker's vocabulary outside). It cannot live anywhere else: clause (a) of the single-writer property says every `work` write is under `work/`, and it is deliberately NOT in `store.ts`, because clause (b) says `work.state` UPDATEs live only there — putting the attribute patcher beside the state writer is exactly the two-mechanism shape the split exists to prevent. Its sibling `tracker-view.ts` (350) is under the cap and stays unlisted. Both shrink at T8c (the schedule and stamp families collapse) and again at T10.

NINE lines, and eight of them are the argument. T8b routed the dashboard's task PUT through `transition()`, which brought G7 (`done` means DELIVERED) onto that path for the first time; `setTaskStatus` returns null on a refusal and this handler ignored the null. Measured on the box before the fix: PUT {status:'complete'} on a task with no resolvable delivery answered HTTP 200 {ok:true} with the UNCHANGED task, and then wrote a `task_log` transition entry saying it moved to complete. A false receipt in the one history the owner reads is worse than the refusal it hid. The refusal now returns 409 carrying the gate's own name and detail, and the audit entry is not written for a move that did not happen. The lines cannot live elsewhere: the verdict has to be read where the response is composed. They come back down at T10 with the route's remaining legacy shims.

PHASE-2 T8V: the verb collapse. 24 public tool names became six `work_*` verbs, and the 76-site measurement T8b2 stopped on is the reason these five files move: ~20 engine behaviours decided what a call MEANT by matching its NAME, and after the collapse a name no longer identifies an operation. Every one of those sites therefore rekeys to `toolOpKey(name, args)` — the operation id, derived in ONE new module (`tools/work-verbs.ts`) and nowhere else. The lines are the rekeys plus the reason each set is an OPERATION set and not a name set, which is the part a future reader needs and cannot re-derive. What the whole change BUYS, stated once: `agent/tools.ts` loses 270 lines (24 tool definitions -> 6, 24 dispatch case labels -> operation labels, one merged edit body), the retired 24 names exist only as alias rows that SWEEP-F T7 deletes, and the PM overseer gate — which a name-only match could no longer express, because `work_update` performs both the close the PM may do and the status flip it may not — states its rule as operations instead of relying on the old one-name-per-operation accident. Nineteen name-matching gates rekeyed (the close-out gate and its satisfaction, the thrash-gate clear, the multi-step floor's two counters and its disarm rule, the start-ack, the add-notes nudge, the bookkeeping nudge, the promise floor, countsAsTaskWork, transitionedThisTurn) plus three named operation sets and `argsForResult`. The helper is the load-bearing addition: a tool RESULT carries no arguments, so the four result-side gates would otherwise have no way to tell a `work_update` status flip from a `work_update` list. It cannot live in work-verbs.ts — it walks the loop's own turn state. AS-BUILT: 9569, not 9614 — the three op sets moved to tools/work-verbs.ts so they could be tested from a leaf, so the file grew by 13 lines rather than 58.

A NEW file past the 240-line visibility threshold, pinned deliberately so the addition is argued rather than noticed later. It is the ONE place a (tool name, arguments) pair becomes the operation it performs. It has to exist and it has to be single: the verb collapse took 24 tool names — each of which identified exactly one operation, which is why ~20 engine behaviours could decide things by matching a name — down to six verbs where the name no longer identifies anything. Every one of those behaviours now asks THIS module, so 'one matcher per marker' still holds; the alternative is the same discriminator ladder re-derived at nineteen call sites, which is the two-mechanism disease with nineteen copies. Roughly half the file is the 23-operation table with the retired verb each absorbed named on its own line, which is what makes the collapse auditable without leaving the file, and the absorb-don't-refuse ladders (#77) that carry the weak-model forgiveness the retired verbs' own handlers held. It SHRINKS at SWEEP-F T7, when the alias rows go and the shape-inference fallbacks stop having to cover old call shapes.
